title: Friday, September 11, 2026

headline.title: CPI landed right on script and the pressure valve finally hissed. August CPI rose 0.4% on the month and 3.4% year-over-year, with core +0.3% monthly and 2.4% annually — in line across the board. The internals are the oil war in one line again: energy +2.1% and gasoline +3.9% on the month, over a third of the entire monthly increase and +27.4% on the year, while food rose just 0.1% and shelter 0.3%. The underlying trend is behaving; the pump is doing the inflating. Today is September 11th — twenty-five years on — and the exchanges will pause for moments of silence this morning.
headline.summary: And Oracle gave the AI trade its answer. Revenue $19.3B, +30%, EPS $1.92 against ~$1.73, cloud infrastructure $7.4B, +121%, and the number that matters: RPO backlog now $664B, up $209B year-over-year, with over $30B of new AI cloud contracts booked in the quarter and full-year guidance raised to at least $90B. It sold off 5.4% with the tape during the session and reversed the entire conversation after hours — premarket 163.00, +6.58%. Oil is exhaling with it: WTI back under $100 and Brent near $104 from Thursday's $107.6, on reports Gulf foreign ministers aim to meet Iran Monday to reopen Hormuz.

overview: Read the release and the reaction together, because they disagree about what matters. CPI came in on consensus — +0.4% headline, 3.4% year-over-year, core 2.4% — and after Thursday's hot PPI, in-line is its own relief. But it is not a number that argues the Fed out of the corner: this was the last inflation read before the FOMC decides September 15-16, markets still price roughly a 70% chance of a 25bp hike under Chair Warsh, and the 2-year sits at its highest in over two years. Thursday made it four straight down days, leaving the S&P about 1.6% and the Dow about 2.5% lower on the week coming in. Both dials pushed: Brent surged over 6% and briefly topped $108 after Iran targeted vessels in the Strait and Houthi forces seized a key Yemeni port, diesel printed an all-time high near $6, the 10-year reached ~4.95% and the 30-year ~5.36%. The ECB hiked 25bp to 2.50% and Lagarde called it a “no brainer” with more priced. This morning both dials ease at once, which is why the gapper board leans green 19 to 5. The honest caveat: a Hormuz reopening changes the oil price, it does not un-print the energy already in the pipe, and gasoline is still +27.4% year-over-year.

Then the number: revenue $19.3B (+30%) against ~$19.1B expected, EPS $1.92 vs ~$1.73, cloud infrastructure $7.4B, +121%, and an RPO backlog of $664B, up $209B year-over-year, with over $30B of new AI cloud contracts booked in the quarter and the full-year guide raised to at least $90B. Premarket 163.00 is above Thursday's entire range. Over 159.24 completes the reversal. The caveat this book has earned the right to state: ORCL gapped once already this week and handed it all back inside a session. The backlog question is now answered — the price is not.

Thursday was a 2 Up entirely above Wednesday — H 158.88 / L 152.48 — closing 158.38 near its high, +5.63%, with Brent over 6% and briefly above $108. Premarket 153.89 gives back half. The cause is exactly the risk carried in every energy write-up this week: Gulf foreign ministers are reportedly aiming to meet Iran on Monday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and WTI is back under $100 with Brent near $104. Under 152.48 the 2 Up fails outright. What complicates the short side is that nothing physical has changed — Houthis hold Mokha, the IEA calls refining “stretched to the limit”, diesel is at a record near $6, and shipping names sit at decade highs. This is a headline about a meeting that has not happened.

It took five sessions and the event itself, but Thursday AAPL reclaimed 317.86 and kept going — a 2 Up taking Wednesday's 319.15 high, running to 326.74, and closing 326.57, +3.56%, three cents off the high on 70.0M shares. That is the downtrend this report tracked all week, ended in one session. Premarket 325.99 is holding it. Thursday's board also carried $239M of AAPL prints around the close. Over 326.74 continues it; the risk is that the move happened the day after the launch rather than on it, which means it is the reaction to the $1,999 Duo pricing rather than the pricing itself — and that reaction has now had one day to be priced.

darkpool.note: The bid-side flip held a second day, and it was emphatic. Thursday's largest single print on the whole tape was IVV $1.8B (bid) — the biggest index print of the week — and overnight the index money kept coming with IVV $1.0B (bid, AH) and VOO $898M (bid, AH). Underneath sat a fixed-income wall stacked the night before CPI: munis in VTEB $633M (ask), SCMB $621M (bid) and MUB $161M (bid), plus DBMF $456M (ask) and AGG $198M (ask) — rate money repositioning into the print with the sides split. The mega-cap baton passed again: after NVDA topped the ex-ETF board three straight sessions, Thursday's largest single name was META $644M (mixed), the third different mega cap up top in three days. And cumulative flow was a size-without-a-side day — MU $2.9B, AAPL $2.6B and SNDK $2.2B, every one of them mixed, with the memory complex over $5B combined and Apple's flow riding a +3% session. The one to sit with is SPCX: a $301M print at the mid after hours, the largest on the board and its third giant flag in a week, landing as headlines crossed a new $1.11B-a-month AI-hosting deal starting December 1 — stacked on Anthropic at $1.25B/month and Google at $920M/month for over $3.4B a month of AI compute by December.

tts.label: Premarket
tts.text: Friday September eleventh, premarket. The headline this report has named as the trade ender every single day this week is arriving. Reports that Gulf foreign ministers are aiming to meet Iran on Monday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz have oil in retreat. U S O is down two point eight three percent after a five point six three percent Thursday, Exxon down zero point nine seven, Chevron down zero point eight one. And the rest of the tape is up on it, with S P Y up zero point seven five percent, Q Q Q up zero point eight three and I W M up zero point seven nine. The second engine is Oracle, and it is violent. It fell five point three eight percent Thursday into its own print, closing one fifty two ninety four on a clean two down, then beat by eighteen cents, guided F Y twenty seven earnings above consensus and told the call it anticipates ninety to ninety five billion dollars of capital expenditure for F Y twenty seven. Premarket one sixty three, up six point five eight percent, back above Thursday's entire range. Add a Bloomberg report that Microsoft is aiming to triple its data center capacity and the A I capex trade has its confirmation. C P I landed at seven thirty central and the tape read it benign.

tts.label: Setups
tts.text: Three setups. First, Oracle, tier one, long. Thursday was a clean two down entirely below Wednesday, high one fifty nine twenty four, low one fifty two fifty two, closing one fifty two ninety four on fifty six point eight million shares, down more than five percent into its own print. Then it beat. Over one fifty nine twenty four completes the reversal and premarket is already well through. The caveat this book has earned the right to state is that Oracle gapped once already this week and handed the whole thing back inside a session. A six point six percent premarket in a name that just fell five point four is a round trip, not yet a trend. Second, U S O, tier one, and this one is flagged red. Thursday was a two up closing near its high, up five point six three percent, the strongest session of the entire oil move. Premarket gives back half of it on the Hormuz reopening report. Under one fifty two forty eight the two up fails outright. What complicates the short side is that nothing physical has changed. The Houthis took Mokha, the I E A calls refining stretched to the limit, and diesel is at a record six dollars six cents. This is a headline about a meeting that has not happened yet. Third, Apple, and the level finally broke. Thursday it reclaimed three seventeen eighty six and kept going, closing three twenty six fifty seven, three cents off its high.

tts.label: Levels
tts.text: The levels that matter today. Oracle, one fifty nine twenty four, Thursday's high, and premarket one sixty three is through it. U S O, one fifty two forty eight, Thursday's low, and below that the two up fails outright. Apple, three twenty six seventy four, Thursday's high, with premarket three twenty five ninety nine holding just under the breakout. S P Y, seven sixty ten, Thursday's high, already reclaimed premarket, and seven sixty sixty four was Thursday's low. Meta, six sixty three fifty, Thursday's outside bar high, and it closed in the lower half of that bar after a six and a half percent run, which is distribution until proven otherwise. Exxon, one sixty three eighteen on the downside of its outside bar. Adobe has no level at all, down three point four percent on a beat, with the freemium push and slower R P O growth clouding the A I progress story. And Micron has now failed at one thousand dollars twice in four sessions, though South Korea's chip exports up two hundred seventy percent is the reason to think a third attempt could be different. Remember this is a Friday into a weekend, with the Hormuz talks Monday and the F O M C decision Wednesday priced near seventy percent for a hike.
